description:
TRAJECTORY.EXE is a team of five aerospace engineering students passionate about space exploration, innovation, and problem-solving. We aim to combine science, technology, and creativity to build engaging solutions that inspire the next generation of space explorers. Our mission is to think boldly, learn continuously, and turn ideas into impact.
From ideas to Orbit.
summary:
LUNAR FRONTIER – Junior Astronaut Adventure Academy is an interactive, browser-based educational experience designed to introduce students aged 7–12 to space science and astronaut training. It transforms traditional learning into an engaging adventure through interactive lessons, astronaut training activities, quizzes, lunar exploration missions, and achievement-based progression.

Players explore the challenges of space exploration, learn scientific concepts, make mission-related decisions, and develop problem-solving skills while progressing through their astronaut journey.

Our goal is to make space education accessible, engaging, and practical for young learners by combining interactive technology, educational content, and mission-based learning.
details: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational space game and learning platform for students aged 7-12, built by team TRAJECTORY.EXE for the NASA Space Apps challenge. It has two parts: Astronaut Academy, which teaches through short lessons, quizzes, a zero-gravity simulator and ORBIT, an AI mentor, with achievements and a leaderboard, and Outpost Command, a playable lunar outpost game where students balance life support, radiation shielding, power and food production. Our Outpost Intelligence Engine links these four systems, so one decision affects all the others. More crew raises air, power and food demand, and stronger shielding costs mass and power. Students learn systems thinking and trade-offs by seeing the consequences of their choices. Game values are grounded in NASA lunar data and sources, including LRO, LROC, LOLA, Diviner, the Planetary Data System, Moon Trek and the NASA Technical Reports Server, with a provenance record and science validation document showing where each value comes from. Our goal is to make space science hands-on, so students can train today and explore tomorrow.
dataRefs: Space-themed STEM content often oversimplifies the engineering trade-offs that define a real mission or presents them at a level too complex to hold a young learner's attention. Few tools make those trade-offs both tangible and fun. Your challenge is to design and build an interactive game or app that lets students run a lunar or Martian outpost, balancing competing demands like life support, radiation shielding, power, and food production, so they experience firsthand the decisions that determine whether a mission fails or succeeds.
